https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Interest payment, in any kind except cash, distributed to holders of an interest bearing asset. SWIFT = PINK

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest payment with principal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: A payment of a portion of the principal of an interest bearing asset, in addition to the interest payment. SWIFT = PRII

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate adjustment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Scheduled change to the coupon rate for a floating or adjustable rate security.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: intermediate securities distribution
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action involving the distribution of intermediate securities or privilege that gives the holder the right to take part in a future event

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: listing status delisting message
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Security is no longer able to comply with the listing requirements of a stock exchange and is removed from official board quotation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: odd lot offer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Offer by issuer to allow holders of an odd lot of a security to order a commission-free transaction at market price, to sell the odd lot, or to buy an amount of shares which will bring the position to a round lot (board lot). SWIFT = ODLT

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: pari-passu action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that occurs when securities with different characteristics become identical in all respects

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: partial redemption with reduction of nominal value action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves redemption of securities in part before their scheduled final maturity date with reduction of the nominal value of the securities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: partial redemption without reduction of nominal value action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves redemption of securities in part before their scheduled final maturity date with no reduction in nominal value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: post-merger securities exchange
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves the exchange of outstanding securities, initiated by the issuer which may include options, as the result of two or more companies combining assets, that is, an external, third party company

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: put redemption action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action involving early redemption of a security at the election of the holder subject to the terms and condition of the issue with no reduction in nominal value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: redemption at maturity action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves redemption of an entire issue outstanding of securities at final maturity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: redenomination action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action by which the unit (currency and/or nominal) of a security is restated

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: repurchase offer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action in which an offer is made to existing shareholders by the issuing company to repurchase equity or other securities convertible into equity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: reverse stock split
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action involving a decrease in a company's number of outstanding equities without any change in the shareholder's equity or the aggregate market value at the time of the split

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rights exercise event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Exercising the right to purchase the shares. Furhter Notes: This is an action on the part of the holder. SWIFT: Call/exercise on nil-paid securities/rights resulting from a rights distribution (RHDI) (To be used for the second event in case rights issue is dealt with in 2 events, first event being the RHDI).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: shares premium dividend action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that pays shareholders an amount in cash issued from the shares premium reserve

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: stock dividend action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves distribution of a dividend to shareholders in the form of equities of the issuing corporation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: stock split
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action involving an increase in a corporation's number of outstanding equities without any change in the shareholder's equity or the aggregate market value at the time of the split

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: tender offer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action involving an offer made to shareholders, normally by a third party, requesting them to sell (tender) or exchange their equities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: trading status active message
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Trading in security has commenced or security has been re-activated after a supsension in trading.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: trading status message
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: A message about trading status.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: trading status suspended message
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: Trading in the security has been suspended.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: warrant exercise action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that offers holders the option to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) a specific amount of stock, cash, or commodity, at a predetermined price, during a predetermined period of time (which usually corresponds to the life of the issue)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: worthless security action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: corporate action that involves booking out of valueless securities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: maturity extension
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event involving extension of payments beyond the original maturity date of the obligation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: asset-backed credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap whose underlying reference obligation is an asset-backed security rather than corporate credit

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap that references a bespoke, synthetic portfolio of underlying assets whose components have been agreed to for a specific OTC derivative by the parties to the transaction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket of credit default swaps
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of reference obligations are credit default swap instruments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cash settlement method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: strategy for calculating or otherwise establishing a reference final price for the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: contingent credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap in which an additional triggering event is required

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: bilateral contract in which one party (protection seller) agrees to provide payment to the other party (protection buyer) should a credit event occur against the underlying, which could be a specified debt (the reference obligation), a specific debt issuer (reference entity), a basket of reference entities and/or reference obligations, or a credit index (reference index)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit default swap index
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: index whose underlying reference obligations are credit default swap instruments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit event notice
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: irrevocable written or verbal notice that states that a triggering event has occurred

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit protection terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: legal terms that define triggering events and associated conditions related to settlement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: deliverable asset
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: asset that must be delivered as a part of the process of settling a credit default swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: deliverable obligation buyer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract party that is obliged to purchase a deliverable obligation (asset) if a triggering event occurs, depending on the event and the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: deliverable obligation seller
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract party that is obliged to sell a deliverable obligation (asset) if a triggering event occurs, depending on the event and the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: escrow agent
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: third party that holds an asset or funds before they are formally transferred from one party to another party, per the terms of a contract, within some specified time period and/or when a triggering event occurs

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap that references a family of standardized credit derivative indices, where the underlying reference entities are a defined basket of credit from a particular geographic region (e.g. Asia, North America, Europe), and/or credit rating level (e.g. emerging markets, high yield, investment grade)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index tranche credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap that references a synthetic collateralized debt obligation (CDO) based on a credit index where each tranche references a different segment of the loss distribution of the underlying index

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: loan credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap whose underlying reference obligation is limited strictly to syndicated secured loans, rather than any type of corporate debt

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: multi-name credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap that references more than one obligation or borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: notifying party
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party responsible for issuing one or more formal notices indicating that an event that is relevant to a given contract has taken place

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: settlement auction
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: independently administered synthetic auction process on a set of defined deliverable obligations that sets the reference final price that can be used to facilitate cash settlement of all covered transactions following a credit event

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: single name credit default swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit default swap whose underlying risk is a single reference obligation, or a single reference entity, such as a corporation or a sovereign borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: triggering event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event that relates to or triggers some aspect of a credit default swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: obligation-specific credit event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event that relates to an individual credit agreement or debt instrument (reference obligation)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cash settlement terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contractual commitment to settle in cash

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: physical settlement terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: commitment to deliver the actual underlying asset on the specified delivery date, rather than cash

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: agricultural resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is obtained via some agricultural process, including forestry, fishing, livestock, grain, dairy, corn, cocoa, soybeans, sugar, coffee

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: base metal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: common metal that tarnishes, oxidizes, or corrodes relatively quickly when exposed to air or moisture, that is widely used in commercial and industrial applications, such as construction and manufacturing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket of commodities
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: custom basket whose constituents consist of one or more negotiable commodities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bullion
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: physical precious metal that is officially recognized as being at least 99.5 percent pure

annotations.example: In the United States, bullion that is eligible for reference in a commodities contract may include U.S. gold Buffalo coins minted by the U.S. Mint that are 1 troy ounce, 0.5 ounce, 0.25 ounce, or 0.10 ounce; 1 ounce silver coins; certain platinum coins; and gold, silver, palladium, and platinum bullion that meet or exceed the fineness requirements of a regulated futures contract. Bullion must also be certified by an approved certifier, typically identified by an exchange, including but not limited to the U.S. Mint.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity basket constituent
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: component of a custom commodity basket whose relative importance with respect to other basket constituents is known

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument whose primary underlying item is a physical commodity, or the price, or related index, or any other aspect related to a physical commodity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity derivative underlier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: underlier of a commodity derivative, including, but not limited to, the negotiable commodity itself

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity forward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: forward contract in which a buyer and seller agree upon delivery of a specified quality and quantity of goods at a specified future date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract to buy or sell a predetermined amount of a commodity at a specific price on a specific date in the future

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity index
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: investment vehicle that tracks a basket of commodities to measure their price and investment return performance

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option where the option buyer has the right to buy or sell specified commodities or commodity related index at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity return leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: leg of a commodity return swap in which the return is based on a physical commodity, or the price, or behavior of the price, or any other aspect related to a physical commodity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity spot contract
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract that involves physical delivery of the commodity asset at settlement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: commodity derivative that includes, without limitation, any swap for which the primary underlying notional item is a physical commodity, or the price, or behavior of the price, or the level of a commodity index, or other aspect related to a physical commodity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: energy resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is an energy-related product, or a derivative of an energy-related product, including electricity, renewable energy, or any power/energy delivered through a utility network of provider; diesel fuel, fuel oil, gas oil, gasoline, heating oil, jet fuel, kerosene, natural gas, oil (Brent, Tapis, Dubai, WTI)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: energy transmission rights
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rights to the transmission of power across an electricity distribution network

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: environmental resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity including offset credits

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: extraction resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is a mineral resource obtained via withdrawal from the natural environment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fertilizer resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that includes ammonia, diammonium phosphate (DAP), potash, sulphur, urea, urea and ammonium nitrate (UAN)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: freight resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is a freight index route

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: gas commodity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: extraction resource that is natural gas

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: generated resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity obtained via some generation process, including electricity, renewable energy, or any power/energy delivered through a utility network or provider

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: grain commodity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: agricultural resource that is a small, hard seed, of a food plant, especially of a cereal plant, such as wheat, corn, rye, oats, rice, and millet

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: industrial resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is obtained via some industrial process, including construction and manufacturing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: meat commodity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: agricultural resource derived from the flesh of an animal (especially a mammal), such as pork bellies

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: metal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: material that, when freshly prepared, polished, or fractured, shows a lustrous appearance, and conducts electricity and heat relatively well

annotations.example: Examples include precious or industrial metal, such as aluminium, copper, gold, lead, nickel, platinum, silver, tin, zinc.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: oil commodity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: generated resource that is a viscous liquid derived from petroleum, including for use as fuel, or as a lubricant, and the manufacture of many types of paints, plastics, and other materials

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: oil grade
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: measure of the viscosity of oil during operation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: paper resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity that is a paper product, including containerboard, newsprint, pulp, recovered paper

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: polypropylene resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity including plastics

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: service resource
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: negotiable commodity involving services such as transportation, communications, and trade

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: weather derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument whose primary underlying notional item is based on something related to the weather, for example, the average temperature in Chicago in January

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: precious metal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: metal that is considered to be rare and/or have a high economic value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: agreement to deliver and settle a given amount of money in one currency, in exchange for a given amount in another currency at an agreed rate of exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency forward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: agreement to deliver and settle a given amount of money in one currency, in exchange for a given amount in another currency, at an agreed date in the future and at an agreed rate of exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency forward outright
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: forward contract in a foreign exchange market that locks in the price at which an entity must buy or sell a currency on a future date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell currency at a specified exchange rate during a specified period of time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency spot contract
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: foreign-exchange contract for immediate delivery

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency spot forward swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: foreign exchange agreement between two parties involving an exchange of two currencies at agreed fixed rates: a) on the spot settlement date and b) a reverse exchange on a later specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: foreign exchange agreement between two parties to exchange a given amount of one currency for another currency for spot delivery or for forward delivery at an agreed rate after a specified period of time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency volatility option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: currency option whose underlying asset is based on the volatility of a foreign exchange rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: foreign exchange master agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: product-specific master agreement intended to reflect best market practice and to provide a standard agreement for participants in the foreign exchange markets

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: foreign exchange settlement netting provision
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: settlement netting provision that is specific to foreign exchange contracts

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is an agreement to exchange a specified amount of one currency for another at some point in the future based on pricing stated in the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cashflow expression
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: expression that specifies a calculation of a cash flow as a component of a cashflow formula

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cashflow formula
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: formula for determining cashflows for a derivative instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cashflow terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: terms setting out a cashflow structure of payments committed to by one party to a contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: contract for difference
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: cash-settled derivative where the parties agree to exchange on the maturity of the contract the difference between the current value of the underlying asset and the initial value of that asset when the contract is initiated

annotations.example: For example, suppose the initial price of share XYZ is $100 and a CFD for 1000 shares is exchanged. Both the buyer and seller must post some margin. If the price goes to $105, then the buyer gets $5,000 from the seller. If the price goes to $95, the buyer pays the seller $5,000. This contract avoids ownership of the stock and all the associated transactions issues (like stamp taxes). The contract also allows for leverage (typically 10:1) because the margin that must be posted is only a fraction of the value of the underlying asset.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument that is a privately held, negotiable bilateral contract traded over-the-counter (OTC) between two parties in a creditor/debtor relationship, enabling the creditor to effectively transfer some or all of the risk of a debtor defaulting to a third party

annotations.example: Examples include credit default swaps (CDS), collateralized debt obligations (CDO), total return swaps, and credit spread options and forwards.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivative settlement terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: settlement terms specifying additional details with respect to what is to be delivered when, to whom, under what conditions at the time of settlement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivative terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contractual terms specific to derivative contracts, including terms related to payments and delivery between parties

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivatives clearing organization
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: clearing house that enables parties to substitute the credit of the DCO for the credit of the parties

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: economic rate-based derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rate-based derivative whose underlier is some economic indicator

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: forward rate agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: agreement to exchange an interest rate commitment on a notional amount at a future date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rate-based derivative whose underlier is an interest rate

annotations.example: For example, interest rate derivative strategies are the simultaneous trading of two or more rate contracts in which two counterparties agree to exchange interest rate cash flows on defined dates during an agreed period, based on a specified notional amount, from a fixed rate to a floating rate, floating to fixed, fixed to fixed, or floating to floating.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: introducing broker
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: broker that solicits or accepts orders for derivatives that are traded on or subject to the rules of an exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: observable value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: specification for the value for something discernible and for which evidence can be obtained

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: over-the-counter derivative instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument that is not listed on an organized exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: over-the-counter instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument and bilateral contract that is not listed on an organized exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: parametric cashflow terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: terms for a set of cashflows defined according to a mathematical formula

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: paying party
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party responsible for making payments in a transaction specified in a contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rate-based derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument where the holder has the right but may not have the obligation, depending on the nature of the instrument, to enter into the underlying contract, or pay or receive payment related to the underlying financial rate (or rate contract) on a specified future date based on a specified future rate and term

annotations.example: Examples of rate-based derivatives include interest rate swaps, forward rate agreements (FRAs), and interest rate options such as caps, floors, and collars.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: receiving counterparty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party that receives payments in a transaction specified in a contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: underlying asset valuation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: assessment activity to estimate the value of an underlying asset of a derivative

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: unique product identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: sequence of characters uniquely identifying an OTC derivative product that is reportable to a trade repository

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: unique product identifier registry entry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entry in a unique product identifier registry

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: unique product identifier service provider
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: organization designated by an external body of financial regulators to assign UPIs and operate a UPI reference data library

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: valuation terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms specific to valuation of the underlying asset(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivative instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument that confers on its holders certain rights or obligations, whose value is derived from one or more underlying assets

annotations.example: The three major categories of derivatives are (1) forward and future contracts, (2) options contracts, and (3) swaps. The most common underlying assets include stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies, interest rates and market indexes.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: underlier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: something that can be assigned a value in the marketplace that forms the basis for a derivative or pool-backed instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: account change notification obligation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: obligation to notify a counterparty of any changes in account details

annotations.example: Example text: "Either party may change its account for receiving a payment or delivery by giving notice to the other party at least five Local Business Days prior to the scheduled date for the payment or delivery to which such change applies unless such other party gives timely notice of a reasonable objection to such change." Note that the notice period is given as a fact about the general kind of obligation which is Master Agreement Change notification Obligation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivative credit support agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: addendum to the master agreement that governs the exchange of collateral between parties in derivatives transactions

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derivative master agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: master agreement covering derivatives transactions to be carried out between the parties to this contract

annotations.example: Related to conditions precedent that may apply: "Each obligation of each party under Section 2(a)(i) is subject to (1) the condition precedent that no Event of Default or Potential Event of Default with respect to the other party has occurred and is continuing, (2) the condition precedent that no Early Termination Date in respect of the relevant Transaction has occurred or been effectively designated and (3) each other applicable condition precedent specified in this Agreement. " In the above, the Obligations defined under Section 2(a)(i) of the Master Agrement is the obligation to make each payment or delivery defined in a Confirmation for a transaction carried out under this Master Agreement.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: master agreement early termination right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contractual right of a party to the master agreement to terminate the agreement early

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: Asian option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option whose exercise terms involve a payoff determined by the average underlying price (either the strike price or the settlement price) of the underlying asset over a predetermined period

annotations.example: For an Asian call option using arithmetic averaging and a 30-day period for sampling the data: On Nov. 1, a trader purchased a 90-day arithmetic call option on stock XYZ with an exercise price of $22, where the averaging is based on the value of the stock after each 30-day period. The stock price after 30, 60, and 90 days was $21.00, $22.00, and $24.00. The arithmetic average (mean) is (21.00 + 22.00 + 24.00) / 3 = 22.33. The profit is the average minus the strike price 22.33 - 22 = 0.33 or $33.00 per 100 share contract. As with standard options, if the average price is below the strike price, the loss is limited to the premium paid for the call options.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: Asian option classifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument classifier that classifies Asian options based on whether they are rate-based or price based

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: averaging strategy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: method used for calculating the average rate or price of an Asian option

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option whose final exercise depends upon the path taken by the price of an underlying instrument, i.e., whose payoff depends on whether or not the underlying asset has reached or exceeded a predetermined price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: chooser option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that allows its holder (buyer) to exercise the right to buy (call) or sell (put) specified assets at a fixed price whereby the buyer does not have to decide whether the contract will be a put or a call until an agreed future date, prior to expiration

annotations.example: For example, assume a trader wants to have an option position for the updated XYZ Inc. earnings release. They think the stock will have a big move, but they are not sure in which direction. The earnings release is in one month, so the trader decides to buy a chooser option that will expire about three weeks after the earnings release. They believe this should provide enough time for the stock to make a significant move if it is going to make one, and fully digest the earnings release. Therefore, the option they choose will expire in seven to eight weeks. The chooser option allows them to exercise the option as a call if the price of XYZ rises, or as a put if the price falls. At the time of the chooser option purchase, XYZ is trading at $28. The trader chooses an at-the-money strike price of $28 and pays a premium of $2 or $200 for one contract ($2 x 100 shares). The buyer can't exercise the option prior to expiry since it is a European option. At expiry, the trader will determine if they will exercise the option as a call or put. Assume the price of XYZ at the time of expiry is $31. This is higher than the strike price of $28, therefore the trader will exercise the option as a call. Their profit is $1 ($31 - $28 - $2) or $100. If XYZ is trading between $28 and $29.99 the trader will still choose to exercise the option as a call, but they will still be losing money since the profit is not enough to offset their $2 cost. $30 is the breakeven point on the call. If the price of BAC is below $28, the trader will exercise the option as a put. In this case, $26 is the breakeven point ($28 - $2). If the underlying is trading between $28 and $26.01 the trader will lose money since the price didn't fall enough to offset the cost of the option. If the price of BAC falls below $26, say to $24, the trader will make money on the put. Their profit is $2 ($28 - $24 - $2) or $200.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cliquet option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that is a series of at-the-money (ATM) options, either puts or calls, where each successive option becomes active when the previous one expires

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodore option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option consisting of a number of digital barrier options that pay a coupon if a pre-determined level of the underlying or basket of underlyings is reached

annotations.example: A three-year commodore option with annual barriers would have three potential payoffs. The first would pay at the end of the first year and would be dependent on the pre-determined barrier being reached or exceeded. For example, if the underlying or basket of underlyings reached or exceeded 102% of its initial level at the end of year one, a coupon of 6% would be paid. At the end of year two, if the underlying reached or exceeded 104% of its initial level, another 6% coupon would be paid. The coupon in the final year would be 6% if the underlying reached or exceeded 106%. The coupon should exceed the performance level of the underlying, otherwise the investor would achieve the same result by investing directly in the underlying.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: compound option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option for which the underlying asset is another option

annotations.example: For example, assume an investor wants to buy a put to sell 100 shares of stock at $50. The stock is currently trading at $55. The investor could buy a Call-Put, which allows them to buy a call now, for say $1 per share ($100), which will allow them to buy a put with a $50 strike in the future. They pay the $1 per share now, but only need to pay the fee for the second option if they exercise the first resulting in them receiving the second option.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: digital option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that has a pre-determined payout if the option is in-the-money and the payoff condition is satisfied

annotations.example: For example, let's say the ABC Index is trading at a level of 2,795 on June 2. An investor believes the ABC Index will trade above 2,800 before the end of the trading day, June 4th. The trader purchases 10 ABC Index options at a strike price of 2,800 options for $40 per contract. If the ABC Index closes above 2,800 at the end of the trading day on June 4, the investor is paid $100 per contract, which is a profit of $60 per contract or $600 (($100 - $40) x 10 contracts). However, if the ABC Index closes below 2,800 on June 4. The investor loses all of the premium amount or $400 ($40 x 10 contracts).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: double barrier option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: barrier option applied to currencies or over the counter stocks that works as a binary, or digital option in that it pays out only under defined circumstances, or it is worthless, at expiration

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed lookback strike expression
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: cashflow expression specifying the arguments required to calculate the fixed price at which the lookback option is to be exercised

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: floating lookback strike expression
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: cashflow expression specifying the arguments required to calculate the best projected price at which the lookback option may be exercised

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: forward start option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that is fully specified with respect to a set expiry date, underlying asset and other parameters, purchased and paid for on initiation, but that becomes active at a set activation date with a strike price determined at the time of activation

annotations.example: For example, assume that two parties agree to enter into a call forward start option on XYZ stock. It is September and they agree that the forward start option will activate on January 1 at the money. That means on January 1 the strike price for the option will be the price that stock is trading at on that day. The option will expire in June. The exact strike price is unknown, but the parties do know the strike and underlying's price will be the same at activation. They can look at current six-month options (January to June) and assess volatility to determine a premium for the option. They agree to trade one contract, equivalent to 100 shares of the underlying stock. They decide on a premium of $40, or $4,000 for the contract ($40 x 100 shares). The call buyer agrees to pay the $4,000 now (September), even though the option doesn't activate till January. On January 1, assume the stock price is $400. The strike is set at $400, and an option is now a vanilla option with a June expiry. At the June expiry, assume XYZ is trading at $420. In this case, the option is worth $20 ($420 - $400 strike). If they settle in cash, the buyer receives $2,000, or if they exercise, they receive 100 shares at $400 and can keep them, or sell them at $420 to make $2,000. Notice that this still results in a loss for the buyer, since they paid $4,000 but are only receiving back $2,000. To make money on the call, the price of the underlying needs to move above the strike price plus the premium. Therefore, if the price moves up to $450 by expiration, the option is worth $50 ($450 - $400 strike), and the buyer receives $5,000. That's a net profit of $1,000 over their $4,000 cost. If the underlying is trading below the $400 strike at expiry, the call option expires worthless and the buyer's premium is lost ($4,000 profit to the seller).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate cap option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate derivative in which the buyer receives payments at the end of each period in which the interest rate exceeds the agreed strike price

annotations.example: An example of a cap would be an agreement to receive a payment for each month the LIBOR rate exceeds 2.5%.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate floor option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate derivative in which the buyer receives payments at the end of each period in which the interest rate is below the agreed strike price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: knock-in option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: barrier option that is not triggered until a certain price threshold is met

annotations.example: Assume an investor purchases a knock-in put option with a down Direction, with a barrier price of $90 and a strike price of $100. The underlying security is trading at $110, and the option expires in three months. If the price of the underlying security reaches $90, the option comes into existence and becomes a vanilla option with a strike price of $100. Thereafter, the holder of the option has the right to sell the underlying asset at the strike price of $100, even though it is trading below $90. It is this right that gives the option value. The put option remains active until the expiration date, even if the underlying security rebounds back above $90. However, if the underlying asset does not fall below the barrier price during the life of the contract, the down-and-in option expires worthless. Just because the barrier is reached does not assure a profit on the trade since the underlying would need to stay below $100 (after triggering the barrier) in order for the option to have value.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: knock-out option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: barrier option with a built-in mechanism to expire as worthless if a specified price level in the underlying asset is reached

annotations.example: Assume an investor purchases a Knock-Out call option with a down Direction, also called a 'Down and Out Option', on a stock that is trading at $60 with a strike price of $55 and a barrier of $50. Assume the stock trades below $50, at any time, before the call option expires. Therefore, the down-and-out call option promptly ceases to exist.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: lookback option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that minimizes the uncertainties related to the timing of market entry, providing the holder the advantage of knowing history when determining when to exercise their option

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: lookback strike terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: terms specifying the value of the underlying asset based on analysis during a specific period, typically ending in the maturity of the option, whereby the payoff is determined by comparing the strike price with the value of the selected price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: low exercise price option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option that is a European-style call option with an exercise price of one cent that mimics a futures contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: mountain range option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option based on multiple underlying securities

annotations.example: Mountain range options are named after a series of mountains, each representing a different type of contract. Some of the most common include: (a) Altiplano options: Altiplano options provide investors with the features of both a traditional vanilla option along with a coupon payment, (b) Annapurna options: coupon rates are determined by the performance of the basket's worst-performing security when it drops under a specified range, (c) Everest options: Everest options place a long-term limit on an investor's option while offering a payout based on the lagging performers in the basket, (d) Atlas options: this type of option eliminates both the best - and worst - performing stocks in a basket of securities, and (e) Himalayan options: traders receive a payout based on the basket's best performing stock; payouts are provided on multiple dates.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: observed best value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: observed value of the underlying asset as of some date during the lookback period that is considered the best value from the perspective of the option holder during the lookback period (depending on whether the option is a call or put)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: projected value at maturity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: expected value of the underlying asset at maturity calculated as of some date during the lookback period

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rainbow option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: exotic option linked to the performances of two or more underlying assets

annotations.example: A best of assets plus cash rainbow effectively has n + 1 payoff possibilities. If we consider a 2 asset "best of plus cash", the payoff at expiry is a choice between Asset 1, Asset 2, or the predetermined cash amount. There is no strike price and the payoff is given as: Rainbow = max(S1, S2, Cash;T)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swaption
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: over-the-counter option that confers the right but not the obligation, to enter into a swap transaction at some time in the future

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is a basket of securities and/or indices

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bond future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one bond

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt instrument future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one debt instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dividend adjustment period
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: date period used to calculate the difference, if any between an anticipated dividend and the actual dividend distributed in that period

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dividend future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one stock dividend

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity forward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: forward contract to buy or sell the underlying equity stock, equity index, basket of equity stock, equity futures contract, or equity option at a specified future date at the price specified at the outset of the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one equity security, specifically a publicly issued and traded share

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: financial future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract based on underlying assets excluding commodities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: forward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument that is privately negotiated between parties to buy the underlier at a specified future date at the price specified in the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: forward contract adjustment method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: method by which adjustments will be made to the contract should one or more of a number of extraordinary events occur

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: future on future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one (other) futures contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: future on option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one option contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: future on swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one swap contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract whose underlying asset is at least one reference index or economic indicator

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract with an interest-bearing instrument as the underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: money market future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: futures contract with a money market instrument as the underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standardized futures listing terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms established by a derivatives exchange that apply to any listing of a futures contract on that exchange.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standardized futures terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms established by a derivatives exchange that apply to any futures contract traded on that exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument that obligates the buyer to receive and the seller to deliver the assets specified at an agreed price, at some later point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option whose underlying asset is a group, or basket, of commodities, securities, indices, or currencies

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bond option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell (depending on whether it is a call or a put) a bond at a certain price on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: butterfly
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: strategy that combines bull and bear spreads with a fixed risk and capped profit

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: call option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy the assets specified at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capped option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option with an established profit cap or cap price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collar
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option trading strategy that involves buying a downside put and selling an upside call that is implemented to protect against large losses, but which also limits large upside gains

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: condor spread
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: non-directional options strategy that limits both gains and losses while seeking to profit from either low or high volatility

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: covered call
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: call option in which the seller (investor) owns an equivalent amount of the underlying security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying equity assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: exotic option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option that has a non-standard payout structure or other feature

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: extrinsic value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: measure of the difference between the market price of an option, called the premium, and its intrinsic value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fence
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option trading strategy that uses options to limit the range of possible returns on a financial instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed income option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying fixed income assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option that giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to receive a cash payment if market interest rate of a reference rate is higher or lower, depending on the option, than the strike rate of the option

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: intrinsic value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: measure of what an asset is worth, i.e. with respect to its current price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: iron butterfly
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: butterfly strategy that consists of two call options and two put options, three strike prices and the same expiration date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: iron condor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: condor strategy consisting of two puts (one long and one short) and two calls (one long and one short), and four strike prices, all with the same expiration date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: long-term equity anticipation security
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: equity option that allows the holder to buy or sell shares of stock with expiration dates that are longer than one year, and typically up to three years from issue

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: moneyness
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: classifier for a derivative relating its strike price to the price of its underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option holder
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party that owns an option

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option issuer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: issuer granting the rights defined in the option in exchange for some consideration

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option on future
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a specific futures contract at a specified price on or before the option's expiration date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option premium
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: current market price of an option contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option premium formula
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: expression used to calculate the premium based either on the price per option or percentage of the notional amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option trading strategy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: trading tactic involving more than one option type, strike price, or expiration date on the same underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: protective collar
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: collar that consists of a covered call and protective put

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: protective put
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: put option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified at with a strike price equal or close to the current price of the underlying asset, on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: put option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: risk reversal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option trading strategy that consists of being short (selling) an out of the money put and being long (i.e., buying) an out of the money call, both with the same maturity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standardized options terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: standardized contract terms established by a securities or options exchange or by an options clearing entity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: straddle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: neutral option trading strategy that involves simultaneously buying both a put option and a call option for the underlying security with the same strike price and the same expiration date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: strangle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option trading strategy in which the investor holds a position in both a call and a put option with different strike prices, but with the same expiration date and underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: strike price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price at which a lot of the underlying asset may be bought or sold when the contract is exercised

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: strip strategy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: option trading strategy that involves a sequential set of options with periodic reset dates, such that each period between resets behaves like an individual option

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: vanilla option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: common option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: option
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument that grants to the holder either the privilege to purchase or the privilege to sell the assets specified at a predetermined price or formula at or within a time period in the future

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: allotment right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: privileges allotted to existing security holders, entitling them to receive new securities free of charge

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: allotment right formula
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rule applied to calculate the number of securities for an allotment right, typically based on the number of these instruments that the holder holds

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier instrument-based mini-future certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: mini-future certificate that immediately expires if the barrier instrument trading price level is breached during product lifetime

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier underlying mini-future certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: mini-future certificate that immediately expires if the barrier underlying level is breached during product lifetime

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a package or group of assets at a specified price during a specified period

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bond purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's bondholders the right to buy bonds of the firm or bonds of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bond subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing bond holders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: call put warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that either does not specify call or put features, or that explicitly includes both a call and put feature

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: call warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to acquire specific underlying assets during a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: combined instruments purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's holders of multiple securities the right to buy securities of the firm or securities of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: combined instruments subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing holders of multiple securities to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of a commodity during a specified period at a specified price

annotations.example: Commodity Warrants Australia (CWA) sells warrants based on 12 commodities and financial markets - crude oil, gold, silver, live cattle, corn, orange juice, soy, coffee, cocoa, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the NASDAQ Composite Index and the S&P 500 Index.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: common convertible share purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's common, convertible shareholders the right to buy common, convertible shares of the firm or common, convertible shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: common convertible share subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing common convertible shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: common share purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's common shareholders the right to buy common shares of the firm or common shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: common share subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing common shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: constant leverage certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entitlement that combines the structure of an open-end certificate with a leverage option with no fixed term, making leverage available without a term restriction, without a knock-out barrier dependency

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: covered warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued without an accompanying security by a third party that holds as many securities as would be required if all the warrants are exercised

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount in a certain currency at a specified exchange rate during a specified period

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of a debt instrument or related debt observable a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of an equity instrument during a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: exchange-traded warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that is listed on a securities exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: exotic warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right (but not the obligation) to buy (or sometimes sell) an underlying asset under non-standard or complex conditions, often involving additional features not found in a plain vanilla (standard) warrant

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount based on the performance of an index during a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: long mini-future certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: mini-future certificate that typically entitles the holder to acquire specific underlying assets during a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: mini-future certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entitlement that combines the structure of an open-end certificate with a leverage option with no fixed term, making leverage available without a term restriction, and whose payoff depends on whether or not the underlying asset has reached or exceeded a predetermined price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: naked warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued without an accompanying security by a third party that does not hold as many securities as would be required if all the warrants are exercised

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: perpetual warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant without an expiration date, giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a certain strike price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: preferred convertible share purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred, convertible shareholders the right to buy preferred, convertible shares of the firm or preferred, convertible shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: preferred convertible share subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred, convertible shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: preferred share purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred shareholders the right to buy preferred shares of the firm or preferred shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: preferred share subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: private warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that is not tradable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: public warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that may be traded over the counter (OTC) or through an exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: purchase right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: anti-takeover device that gives a prospective acquiree's shareholders the right to buy shares of the firm or shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: put warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified (i.e., acquire cash in exchange for the underlying assets, such as stock) back to the issuer at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: short mini-future certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: mini-future certificate that entitles the holder to acquire cash in exchange for specific underlying assets

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: structured warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that is listed on an exchange, offering investors a way to participate in the price performance of an underlying asset without buying it directly

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: subscription right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: privileges allotted to existing security holders, entitling them to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: traditional warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued by the issuer of the underlying instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entitlement that permits the holder to purchase a specified amount of a financial instrument, commodity, currency or other asset during a specified period at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entitlement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument that provides the holder an interest in, or the privilege to subscribe to, or to receive specific assets under terms specified

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bond with warrant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: bond that is issued together with one or more warrant(s) attached as part of the offer, the warrant(s) granting the holder the right to purchase a designated security, often the common stock of the issuer of the debt, at a specified price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier capital protection certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier discount certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the maximum redemption amount (Cap) is paid out if the barrier is never breached

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: barrier reverse convertible certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the barrier never be breached, the nominal price plus coupon is paid at redemption; if the barrier is breached the product changes into a reverse convertible

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate whose underlying asset represents a fraction of a basket of securities that corresponds to the subscription ratio

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bonus certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with a greater risk in relation to multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of), allowing for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and with a reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

annotations.example: For example: You buy a bonus certificate based on a stock. The price of the stock at the time that you get the certificate is 100 Euros. The bonus level is 120 Euros, and the protection threshold is 80 Euros. Over the two-year term, the price of the stock fluctuates between 90 and 110 Euros. When the certificate matures at the end of the term, you receive the bonus price of 120 Euros.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capital-protected product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: structured product that participates in the performance of a financial asset, such as a stock, fund or index, while protecting the investor's capital

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capital protection certificate with coupons
