https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capital protection certificate with participation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal amount (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capital protection convertible certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: discount certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the underlying asset(s) and/or a cash amount is redeemed should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, for which, in return, the potential profit is capped

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: express certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying trade above the strike on the observation date, an early redemption consisting of nominal price plus an additional coupon amount is paid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate whose underlying asset is an index

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: leveraged product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: structured product that provides a further enhanced yield (over and above that of a yield-enhancement product), often without any limit to the upside participation, and frequently with a stop-loss in order to limit potential capital losses

annotations.example: Leveraged certificates are examples of leveraged products; they provide enhanced participation to an underlying with inbuilt leverage. Leveraged exposure is also provided on the downside performance of the underlying. Another example is a call warrant, which is simply a call option that is traded in a securitized format. This format is interesting in order to be able to trade a call option on underlyings for which no exchange traded option market exists.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: outperformance bonus certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, in which the minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with greater risk multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of) allow for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: outperformance certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, reflecting underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees), and whose risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

annotations.example: For example: You buy an outperformance certificate based on a stock. The certificate’s strike price is 100 Euros and its participation factor is 150 percent. If the price of the underlying stock surpasses the strike price of 100 Euros, you are rewarded with a 150 percent return, instead of just 100 percent. If the price of the stock climbs to 110 Euros, for example, the value of the certificate would be 115 Euros.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: participation certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation product that provides the possibility to participate in the gains or losses in the price of an asset, subject to counterparty risk

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: participation instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: structured product that provides the possibility to participate in the performance of an asset or basket of assets

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: reverse convertible certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, the underlying asset(s) and/ or a cash amount is redeemed; should the underlying asset close above the strike at expiry, the nominal amount plus the coupon is paid at redemption

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: structured product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security whose cash flow characteristics depend upon one or more indices or that have embedded forwards or options or securities where an investor's investment return and the issuer's payment obligations are contingent on, or highly sensitive to, changes in the value of underlying assets, indices, interest rates or cash flows

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: tracker certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate that reflects underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by conversion ratio and any related fees), in which the associated risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

annotations.example: Tracker certificates can be purchased on stock exchanges which they are listed on. Many of these certificates track underlying assets at a ratio of 1:100. That means that an investor can invest just a fraction of the amount which would be required to buy the actual underlying asset. For example: You invest in a tracker certificate which is based on a stock basket with a value of 10,000 Euros. Because the tracker certificate uses a ratio of 1:100, you only need to pay 100 Euros for the certificate. If the price of the underlying stocks goes up by 10 percent (to 11,000 Euros), the value of the certificate will also go up by 10 percent (to 110 Euros).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: turbo certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate that acts as a leveraged security, whose price tracks an underlying financial asset's price one for one, and that can be used to go long or short

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: twin-win certificate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: certificate that makes profits possible with rising and falling underlying asset values, in which a falling underlying asset price converts into profit up to the barrier, and whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: yield-enhancement product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: structured product that provides a predefined yield in return for a downside risk

annotations.example: Well-known yield-enhancement products include reverse convertibles. They provide a predetermined yield per annum in return for the willingness of the investor to absorb downside risk of for example a stock, index, currency-pair or fund. Reverse convertibles come in a broad range of variations (with or without barrier, multiple underlyings and/or callability).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: principal protected note
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: structured finance that offers investors exposure to chosen underlying assets using various approaches and asymmetric pay-off profiles

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: structured finance instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: pool-backed security wherein the risk associated with the pool has been uncoupled from the risk associated with the originating institution through a special purpose vehicle

annotations.example: Collateralized debt obligations (CDOs), synthetic financial instruments, collateralized bond obligations (CBOs), and syndicated loans are examples of structured finance instruments.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basis swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap in which payment streams are referenced to different bases

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: correlation leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg of a correlation swap that pays an amount based on the observed average correlation of the prices of a collection of underlying products

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: correlation swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: over-the-counter statistical derivative that allows one to hedge risks associated with the observed average correlation of a collection of underlying products

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dispersion leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg of a dispersion swap that pays an amount based on the realized dispersion of the price changes of the underlying product

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dispersion swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: statistical derivative used to hedge on the magnitude of a price movement of an underlying asset

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: excess return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return swap in which the change in the level of the index will be equal to the returns generated primarily by the changes in price of each of the contracts that comprise the index

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate or consisting of at least one payment of a fixed amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed payment leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg that specifies contractual terms associated with a schedule of payments for any swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: floating leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to some variable rate, calculated based on the change in value of some underlying asset, or consisting of at least one payment of some floating amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: index return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return swap in which payments are based on a fee paid to the seller of the swap and on a floating reference price based on changes in the level of an index from an initial level to a level observed on some valuation date(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: major swap participant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial service provider that maintains a substantial position in swaps for any of the major swap categories

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: performance-based variable leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg of a swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rate-based leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg of a rate-based swap based on a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rates swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap in two counterparties each agree to pay the other cash flows on defined dates during an agreed period, based on a specified notional amount and a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: realized variable leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: performance-based leg wherein the payment is netted at maturity rather than periodically

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: return leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: leg of a swap in which the income generated by some underlier is paid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap in which one leg, the return leg, is based on income generated from some underlier

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: simple return leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return leg based strictly on the income generated by the underlying asset, excluding appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: statistical swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: strike leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg that specifies a fixed amount, 'the strike', quoted at the time of execution

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument whereby counterparties agree to exchange periodic streams of cash flows or liabilities from two different financial instruments with each other

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap confirmation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: formal confirmation that codifies the terms and conditions specific to a lifecycle event with respect to the overall transaction between the parties

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap data repository
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial service provider that provides a central facility for swap data reporting and recordkeeping

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap dealer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: non-depository institution such as one that deals in swaps, makes a market in swaps, regularly enters into swaps with counterparties as an ordinary course of business for its own account, and engages in any activity causing the person to be commonly known in the trade as a dealer/market maker in swaps

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: terms defining and the commitment to fulfill cashflow requirements (e.g., interest payments, coupon payments, etc.) for a component of a swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap leg event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap lifecycle event, such as a payment or rate reset event, that applies to one leg of a swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap lifecycle event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event that occurs during the lifecycle of a swap, where the overall set of events includes those specific to the issuer, front office, middle office, and/or back office processes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap lifecycle event identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: identifier that uniquely identifies a specific event in the lifecycle of a swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap party
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party to a swap and therefore a legal party to the contract that embodies that transaction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap paying party
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap party responsible for making payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap receiving party
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap party that receives payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: swap terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: legal contractual terms of a swap transaction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: total return leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return leg based on the income generated by the underlying asset as well as any appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: total return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return swap where the seller agrees to pay the other party the difference in value of some underlying asset multiplied by an agreed-upon notional value should the asset value increase between specified periods of time

annotations.example: For example the parties may enter into a two year agreement where every three months they compare the value of the Barclays Capital Aggregate Bond Index to its value three months previously. If the agreed upon notional was US $10,000,000 and the value increased 0.04%, or 4 basis points (bps), the seller would pay the buyer US $4,000. If, after another three months, the value decreased by 3bps, the buyer would pay the seller US $3,000. As part of the agreement, the buyer may also make an additional payment each period to the seller based on a floating rate index multiplied by the notional value.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: unique swap identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: identifier for a swap that is used in recordkeeping and swap data reporting

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cross-currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which the two streams of interest payments are in different currencies

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed fixed interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which both parties pay a fixed interest rate that they could not otherwise obtain outside of a swap arrangement

annotations.example: For example, each counterparty uses a different native currency, but wants to borrow money in the other counterparty's native currency.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed float cross-currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments and the two streams of interest payments are in different currencies

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed float interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed float single currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments and where both payment streams are expressed in terms of the same currency

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed interest rate leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: fixed leg that specifies fixed interest amounts and terms for the payment of that interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: float float cross-currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different interest rates in different currencies

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: float float interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different floating interest rates

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: float float single currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different floating interest rates in the same currency

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: floating interest rate leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg in which variable interest is paid on some notional amount, linked to some underlying interest reference rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: inflation leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating rate leg of an inflation swap linked to an inflation index, such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: inflation swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rate swap in which one party pays an amount calculated using an inflation rate index, and the other party pays an amount calculated using another inflation rate index, or a fixed or floating interest rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap in which the reference (underlier) for at least one leg is an interest rate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate swap leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap leg that has an interest rate payment stream, including both a parametric and cashflow representation for the stream of payments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: notional step amount
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the amount of money that is subtracted from the notional on each step date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: notional step change event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event in which a step change in the notional amount for a given swap leg occurs

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: notional step period length
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: recurrence interval indicating the frequency with which step changes occur, which is a multiple of the calculation period in the calculation schedule

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: notional step schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: schedule of changes in the notional amount on which interest is paid, comprising the regular sequence of step events

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: overnight index swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap in which the periodic payments for one leg are based on an overnight interest rate index multiplied by the same notional amount upon which payments for the other leg of the swap are based

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: overnight rate index leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg in which periodic payments are based on an overnight interest rate index multiplied by the same notional amount on which the payments for the other leg of the swap are based

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: plain vanilla interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: fixed-float single currency interest rate swap in which interest payments are netted, the notional principal does not change, and there are no embedded options

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: single currency interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which the two streams of interest payments are in the same currency

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: zero coupon interest rate swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate swap in which the fixed rate cash flows are compounded and paid once on the expiration date, rather than periodically; the payments on the other side (which can be based on a floating interest rate or a fixed rate) follow typical swap payment schedules

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dispersion swap index constituents leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: dispersion leg whose underlier is a defined set of constituents of a given equity index

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dispersion swap index leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: dispersion leg whose underlier is an equity index

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dividend leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: floating leg of a dividend swap

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dividend swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: equity swap that has at least one leg whose underlier is a dividend stream

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity correlation swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: correlation swap that allows one to hedge risks associated with the observed average correlation of a collection of underlying equity products

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity price return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return swap whose return leg underlier is based on equities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity return leg
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return leg whose income is based on equities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: swap whose payments are linked to the change in value of underlying equities (e.g. shares, basket of equities or index) or their cashflow(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity total return swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: total return swap whose return leg underlier is based on equities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity variance swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: dispersion swap in which the parties agree to exchange payments based on the difference between (i) the realized variance of the price changes of a specified equity underlier over a stated observation period and (ii) a fixed amount of variance that is agreed when the contract is executed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity volatility swap
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: dispersion swap that is a forward contract on the variability of movements in the price of its underlying equities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: qualifying dividend period
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: date period over which the sum of all qualifying dividends paid by the relevant issuers as identified in the swap terms is calculated

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: special dividend leg terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: terms that are invoked if special dividend and memorial dividends are applicable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: basket of debt instruments
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of securities whose constituents are debt instruments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capitalized lease obligation debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments whose constituents are contracts entitling a renter the temporary use of an asset and, in accounting terms, has asset ownership characteristics

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: contribution debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments that allows a company to incur an amount of indebtedness that is equal to (or in top tier sponsor transactions in the U.S., up to two times) the amount of equity contributed to the group

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit facility debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of securities whose constituents are credit agreements that allow the borrower to periodically take out money over an extended period of time rather than reapplying for a loan every time they need funds

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt instrument derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security-based derivative whose underlier is a debt observable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security-based derivative whose underlier is based on equities (e.g. shares, basket of equities or index) or their cashflow(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: general debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments that provides additional capacity for potential funding and does not require the proceeds to be used for any particular purpose

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: incremental facility debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of credit facilities whose constituents are extensible, allowing companies to borrow an additional term loan or revolving credit facility (or increase the commitments applicable thereto) under the same credit agreement subject to certain parameters

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: local lines of credit debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments that may be relevant for companies with international operations, often permitting debt to be incurred by a non-guarantor restricted subsidiary

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: non-guarantor debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments that include a provision allowing certain subsidiaries within a corporate group, which are not part of the loan guarantee, to incur a specified amount of indebtedness

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: ratio debt basket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: basket of debt instruments whose constituents are specified based on a leverage ratio based on total debt rather than only secured debt

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: security-based derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: derivative instrument whose underlier is based on a security, including collections of securities and indices based on securities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bankruptcy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event involving a change in state or condition in which a party becomes insolvent

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event signifying a sudden change in credit standing, such as bankruptcy or a violation of a bond indenture or loan agreement, that raises doubts about the party's ability to meet current or future obligations

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cross default provision
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract provision that triggers a default under one contract if the borrower defaults on another related obligation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: default event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event representing a failure to meet a contractual obligation, such as failure to repay a debt including interest or principal on a loan or security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: distressed ratings downgrade
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event triggered when the credit rating of an obligation is downgraded to a distressed debt level

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: downgrade
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event triggered when the credit rating of a party or obligation is lowered

annotations.example: On October 17, 2013, Dagong Global Credit Rating downgraded the United States from A to A- and maintained a negative outlook on the country's credit.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity-specific credit event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event that applies to a given legal person

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: failure to pay
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event that is triggered following any applicable grace period in which a payment obligation is missed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: failure to pay interest
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event that where either an expected interest payment is missed altogether or the amount paid is less than the required amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: failure to pay principal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event that where either an expected principal payment is missed altogether or the amount paid is less than the required amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: filing for bankruptcy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event that involves a request to a court to be recognized as bankrupt

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: hard credit event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event that is not repairable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: installment default
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event involving non-payment of several installment payments as scheduled in the terms of the agreement, or non-payment of a call by the beneficial owner

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest obligation in light of default
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: obligation in respect of default(s) in the performance of any payment obligation

annotations.example: Prior to the occurrence or effective designation of an early termination date in respect of the relevant transaction, a party that defaults in the performance of any payment obligation will, to the extent permitted by law (and in the case of an ISDA Master Agreement is subject to Section 6(c)), be required to pay interest (before as well as after judgment) on the overdue amount to the other party on demand in the same currency as such overdue amount, for the period from (and including) the original due date for payment to (but excluding) the date of actual payment, at the default rate. Such interest will be calculated on the basis of daily compounding and the actual number of days elapsed.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: moratorium
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entity-specific credit event involving a temporary suspension of payments until related issues are resolved

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: obligation acceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event triggered when one or more reference obligations become immediately due and payable as a result of a default or covenant breach on the reference entity's other debt instruments, subject to a materiality threshold

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: obligation default
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event triggered as a result of an obligation-specific default

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: obligation restructuring
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event that materially impacts an obligation, such as an interest rate reduction, principal reduction, deferral of interest or principal, change in priority ranking, or change in currency or composition of payment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: repudiation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit event involving the refusal to honor the terms of a contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: soft credit event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: default event that is repairable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: write-down
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: obligation-specific credit event whereby the book value of the obligation, such as the outstanding principal amount, is reduced

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit inquiry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: request from a lender to a credit repository to obtain information regarding a prospective borrower's creditworthiness

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit inquiry type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: classifier indicating whether a credit inquiry is a result of a borrower's direct authorization or by some indirect means

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit message
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: notice on a credit report to alert a reviewer of special or exceptional information

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit message type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: classifier that categorizes credit messages

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit quality
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: classifier for borrowers, rates, or holdings in the lending market with respect to the quality of the credit

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit rating
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: assessment of creditworthiness of a borrower generally or with respect to a particular debt or financial obligation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit rating agency
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rating agency that publishes reports assessing the creditworthiness of a borrower or legal entity, either generally or with respect to a specific obligation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit rating model
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: algorithm for computing a credit rating

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit score model type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: a type corresonding to a family of credit scoring algorithms sharing common characteristics

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit rating scale
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: rating scale for assigning a credit rating to individual, entity, or instrument, including defining a set of codes or numeric scores and indicating how an assessment that is assigned a score based on that scale means

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit report
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: report describing the creditworthiness and related credit attributes of a borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit report category
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: classifier for credit reports, often available from multiple vendors

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit report product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: branded credit report offered in the marketplace

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit tradeline
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: report derived from the transaction history of a credit account

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: instrument credit rating
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: investment credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an instrument, typically with some relationship to the creditworthiness of the issuer(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: investment credit rating
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an investment, including but not limited to an instrument or organization

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: organization credit rating
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an organization

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: short term credit rating
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of the probability of an individual or organization going into default within a year

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: accrual
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the process of accumulating interest or other income that has been earned but not paid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: accrued interest
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: amount of interest that has been incurred, as of a specific date, on a loan or other financial obligation but has not yet been paid out

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: amortization
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the process of reduction of debt or other costs through periodic charges to assets or liabilities, such as through principal payments on mortgages

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: amortization schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: schedule of periodic payments (repayment installments) that specify changes in the balance of the debt over time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: borrower
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party to a credit agreement that is obligated to repay the amount borrowed (principal) with interest and other fees according to the terms of the instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: borrower identification scheme
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: system for allocating identifiers to borrowers

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: borrower identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: sequence of characters, capable of uniquely identifying a borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: borrowing capacity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: upper bound on the total amount of money that a lender believes a party has the ability to repay an obligation when due, as of some point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: capital lease
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lease that must be reflected on an organization's balance sheet as an asset and as a corresponding liability

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collateral
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: something pledged as security to ensure fulfillment of an obligation to another party, to lend money, extend credit, or provision securities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collateral value as of date
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: appraised value of the collateral for an obligation as of a given date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: committed credit facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit facility that is a confirmed source of financing for the borrower, as long as the borrower meets the conditions of the agreement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: committed sub-facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contractually committed portion of a credit facility that is available to the borrower and may be associated with some specific collateral

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contractual agreement in which a debtor receives something of value and typically agrees to repay the creditor by some date in the future, in some form (e.g., cash, securities, etc.), generally with interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit agreement repaid at maturity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit agreement in which accrued interest may be periodically repaid or paid at maturity, but principal is paid at maturity

annotations.example: The most common example of a credit agreement repaid at maturity is a bond.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit agreement repaid periodically
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit agreement in which the principal and accrued interest may be periodically repaid or exchanged

annotations.example: Examples include revolving lines of credit, commercial loans, construction loans, residential mortgages and so forth.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit enhancement agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: collateral agreement that governs the exchange of collateral between parties to mitigate counterparty credit risk

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit enhancement beneficiary
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party that benefits from the collateral or guarantee established under the agreement, i.e., that is protected against counterparty credit risk because the collateral or guarantee serves as security for the obligation(s) owed to them

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: credit facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit agreement that allows the borrower to periodically take out money over an extended period of time rather than reapplying for a loan every time they need funds

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: creditor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: a party to whom an obligation, such as an amount of money, or good, or performance of some service exists

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: day-count convention
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: a business recurrence interval convention that is used to calculate the number of days in an interest payment, which applies to the amount of accrued interest or the present value for debt instruments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: obligation to pay something, such as an amount of money, good, service, or instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms that specify the formal rights and obligations of borrower and lender under a contract in which funds are lent from the one party to the other

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debtor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: a party that owes a debt or other obligation to another party

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: explicit contract event schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: schedule of events, including but not limited to payment events, rate reset events and others that will occur over the lifetime of the credit agreement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: fixed interest rate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: interest rate that does not fluctuate over the lifetime of a loan or other debt instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: floating interest rate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: variable interest rate that is based on a specific index or benchmark rate

annotations.example: Certain revolving credit, such as credit-card related debt, may adjust after a specified period of time to an absolute rate stated in the agreement (variable but not floating) rather than based on a benchmark rate (variable, floating).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: full amortization
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: amortization in which the very last payment (which, if the schedule was calculated correctly, should be equal to all others) pays off all remaining principal and interest on the loan

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the cost of using credit, or another's money, expressed as a rate per period of time, payable by a debtor to a creditor in consideration of the credit extended to the debtor

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest calculation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event reflecting the calculation of interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest calculation schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which interest is calculated

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest payment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event reflecting the actual payment of interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest payment schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which interest is due to be paid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest payment terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms for payment of interest on a debt

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate reset
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event reflecting a potential adjustment to an interest rate, typically corresponding to a change in the underlying benchmark interest rate or index specified in the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate reset schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which a rate reset, and corresponding actual rate, is recalculated

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: interest rate setting event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event on which an initial rate for a given contract is set, which may be relative the the occurrence of some other contract lifecycle event, such as the execution date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: lease
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit agreement permitting the use of real estate, equipment or another asset, such as a vehicle, by the owner of that asset (the lessor) to a user (the lessee) for a specific period of time in return for payment as specified in the agreement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: lender
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: a party that extends credit or money to a borrower with the expectation of being repaid, usually with interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: managed interest rate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: variable interest rate charged by a financial institution for borrowing that is not prescribed as a margin over base rate but is set from time to time by the institution

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: motor vehicle lease
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lease of a motor vehicle for a fixed period of time at an agreed amount of money

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: negative amortization
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: amortization in which the payments made do not cover the interest due

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: non-physical collateral
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: asset pledged as collateral that is a financial asset, rather than physical asset

annotations.example: Examples of non-physical collateral include, but are not limited to, bank deposits, accounts receivable, stocks, bonds, other securities, and the like.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: partial amortization
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: amortization in which the very last payment the last payment due may be a large balloon payment of all remaining principal and interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: physical collateral
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: asset pledged as collateral that has a material form, i.e., is a physical asset of the obligor

annotations.example: Examples of physical collateral include, but are not limited to, real estate, equipment, vehicles, spare parts, inventory, goods, supplies, fixtures, and leasehold improvements.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: principal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: with respect to a debt: the value of an obligation, such as a bond or loan, raised and that must be repaid at maturity; for investments: the original amount of money invested, separate from any associated interest, dividends or capital gains

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: principal payment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: event reflecting the actual payment of some amount of the principal of a debt

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: principal payment schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which some percentage or all of the principal is due to be (re)paid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: principal repayment terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms that specify requirements for repayment of the principal

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: projected contract event schedule
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: schedule of events, including but not limited to anticipated payment events, rate reset events and others that are expected to occur over the lifetime of the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rate reset time of day
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: time of day that an interest rate is reset, as indicated by some interest rate authority or market data provider

annotations.example: Examples include certain rates published by the Federal Reserve Board in their H.15 schedule, which are published at 4:15 pm on business days that are not holidays in the US.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: retail credit facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit facility that is a loan or line of credit used by retailers and real estate companies

annotations.example: Most consumer credit cards are retail credit facilities, for example.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: revolving line of credit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit facility that enables the borrower to withdraw funds, repay, and withdraw again

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: security agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: collateral agreement that grants a financial interest in some collateral to a party that is not an owner of that collateral, specifying terms including relative duties and rights, over and above those specified in the primary contract, regarding the disposition of the asset used as collateral

annotations.example: Examples include deeds of trust and uniform commercial code (UCC) agreements.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: sub-facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: portion of a credit facility extended to the borrower for some purpose, possibly per some schedule specified in the facility

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: uncommitted credit facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: credit facility that has yet to be confirmed as a source of financing for the borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: uncommitted sub-facility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: sub-facility that has yet to be confirmed as a source of financing for the borrower

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: variable interest rate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: an interest rate that is allowed to vary over the maturity of a loan or other debt instrument

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collateral agreement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: written contract related to another contract designed to provide clarity and additional protection for all parties involved, that is separate from the primary contract and that can be independently enforced

annotations.example: Examples may be related to leases, to clarify responsibilities with respect to maintance and repair, to partnerships, clarifying how disputes should be resolved, loan agreements such as deeds of trust, covering the conditions under which the collateral would be forfeited, and uniform commercial code (UCC) agreements.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collateralized guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty that takes the form of some asset that is pledged by a borrower to a lender (usually in return for a loan)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: government guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty provided by a government entity, such as for a government-backed security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: guarantor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party that guarantees, endorses, or provides indemnity for some obligation on behalf of some other party

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: commitment whereby something is formally assured if a party with primary liability fails to perform

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: insurance-backed guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty that is realized as an insurance policy

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: insurance policy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract that (1) puts an indemnity cover into effect, (2) serves as a legal evidence of the insurance agreement, (3) sets out the exact terms on which the indemnity cover has been provided, and (4) states associated information such as the (a) specific risks and perils covered, (b) duration of coverage, (c) amount of premium, (d) mode of premium payment, and (e) deductibles, if any

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: insurer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial service provider that issues an insurance policy

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: joint guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty provided by at least two parties, jointly and severally

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: letter of credit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: letter from a bank or other creditworthy institution guaranteeing that a buyer's payment to a seller will be received on time and for the correct amount

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: letter of credit guaranty
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty that takes the form of a letter of credit, i.e., a document issued by a bank guaranteeing the payment up to a stated amount for a specified period

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: negative pledge
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: guaranty whereby the issuer will not pledge any assets if doing so would result in less security for lender(s) or investor(s)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: policyholder
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: counterparty to and typically owner of an insurance policy

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: priority level
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: relative ranking that a guaranty has in the context of a contract, for example for a credit enhancement priority

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: calculation agent
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: party that is responsible for determining the value of an instrument and in some cases, determines how much the parties owe one another

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: cash instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument whose value is determined by the market and that is readily transferable (highly liquid)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: commodity instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument representing an ownership interest in bulk goods, such as raw materials and primary agricultural products

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: currency instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument used for the purposes of currency trading

annotations.example: Example currencies include UK pounds, US dollars, Euro. An example currency instrument is spot currency instrument.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: debt instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument and credit agreement evidencing monies owed by the issuer to the holder on terms as specified

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: equity instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument representing an ownership interest in an entity or pool of assets

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: exempt security
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security that is exempt from certain regulatory rules

annotations.example: Some exemptions from the registration requirement include: private offerings to a limited number of persons or institutions; offerings of limited size; intrastate offerings; and securities of municipal, state, and federal governments.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: financial instrument
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: written contract that gives rise to both a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability of another entity

annotations.example: Examples of financial instruments include: cash, evidence of an ownership interest in an entity, or a contractual right to receive (or deliver) cash, or another financial instrument.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: financial instrument identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: sequence of characters uniquely identifying a financial instrument for some purpose and within a specified context

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: issuer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: role of a party that issues (or proposes to issue in a formal filing) one or more financial instruments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: negotiable security
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security that can be transferred to another party

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: non-negotiable security
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: security that is not transferable to another party

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: packaged financial product
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial product that acts as a container for at least one financial instrument, including other financial products, and whose value is derived from, or based on a reference asset, market measure, or investment strategy

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: promissory note
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: debt instrument that is a written promise by one party to another that commits that party to pay a specified sum on demand or within a specified time frame under specified terms

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: redemption provision
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract provision enabling the issuer (writer) to regain possession through repayment of some stipulated price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: securities transaction
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: transaction between two or more parties involving the exchange of commonly defined financial products

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: security
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument that can be bought or sold

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: spot contract
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: financial instrument that settles for immediate delivery on a specified date

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standardized terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms that, grouped together, that are generally and consistently reused across many contracts, published by some organization, and capable of being incorporated into a contract by reference

annotations.example: Each exchange has a set of terms they apply to membership agreements and with respect to the instruments that may be traded on that exchange. For example, there is a set expiration date that exchanges will publish for exchange-traded options - in the US it is the Saturday following the third Friday of every month. Similarly, there are set incremental dates for strike for exchange traded options. Contract sizes are also stipulated, for example in the US these are standardized by the OPRA Convention (Options Pricing Reporting Authority).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: unique transaction identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: sequence of characters identifying a financial transaction uniquely whenever useful and agreed by the parties or community involved in the transaction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: adjusted closing price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: amended closing price to reflect a security's value after accounting for any corporate actions, such as stock splits, dividends, and rights offerings

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: best bid
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: highest bid price a prospective buyer is willing to pay at a particular time for a given security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: best offer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lowest price acceptable to a prospective seller for a given security at a particular point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bid ask spread
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: difference between an offer (ask) price and a bid price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: bid price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price a prospective buyer is willing to pay

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: clean price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: debt instrument price that does not include accrued interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: closing price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: cash value of the last transacted price before the market closes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: closing price determination method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: strategy for calculating or otherwise determining an official closing price

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: collection of security prices
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: collection consisting of a series of prices, each of which has a specific date and time associated with it, for some security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: composite market
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: group of exchanges and trading venues referenced for pricing purposes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: derived price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price that stems from another source or calculation rather than being quoted or based on actual trading data

annotations.example: For example, a product's price can be derived from another pricing source, such as an asset or product, using various contributing factors. Derived prices can also be calculated within a firm using published price spreads or other market data. An interpolated price is determined by interpolation between available price figures, using some algorithm or curve, such as between bid and offer (among others). It also includes yield curves and implied forward curves. That is, interpolation may either be linear (straight line interpolation between two values) or may be expressed as a non linear curve such as a yield curve or an implied forward curve.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: dirty price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: debt instrument price that includes accrued interest

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: high price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: highest price for a given security over the period specified

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: internal rate of return
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: discount rate that results in a net present value (NPV) of zero for a series of future cash flows

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: intra day price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price for a given security at some point between the opening and official closing price on an exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: low price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lowest value for a given security over the period specified

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: market price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: last reported price at which a security was sold

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: mid price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: arithmetic mean between bid and offer prices

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: offer price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price suggested by a prospective seller at a particular time for a given security

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: official closing price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price of the final trade of a security at the end of a trading day on a given exchange

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: opening price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price at which something first trades at the start of a trading day

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: price analytic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: statistical measure involving security prices

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: price determination method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: strategy for calculating or otherwise establishing a price for something

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: price spread
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: difference between two prices

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: pricing model
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: expression used to determine a value for an instrument at a given point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: rate of return
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: net gain or loss on an investment over a specified time period, expressed as a percentage of the investment's initial cost or value as of a specific point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: security price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: monetary price for a financial instrument at some point in time

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: trading day
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: time span that a particular trading venue is open

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: trading session
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: window of time within a trading day in which orders may be placed and filled

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: volume-weighted average price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: average price at which a given security has traded throughout a trading day, determined by multiplying each trade by its volume, adding the results, then dividing by the volume traded for the day

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: volume-weighted open price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: price determined by multiplying each trade by its volume, adding the results, then dividing by the volume over a certain period during the trading day (rather than over the course of the entire day)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: yield
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: return on the investor's capital investment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: yield spread
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the spread between the yields of two items

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: calculated price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: monetary price determined by a formula

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: delivery method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: method and commitment to transfer a commodity, currency, security, cash or another instrument as defined in the settlement terms of the contract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: settlement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: act of finalizing a transaction, including but not limited to finalizing accounting, exchanging consideration, and/or legally recording documents, as applicable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: settlement convention
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: convention employed to determine the closing date (from the stated settlement date) in the process of settling a transaction on which securities or interests in securities are delivered, usually against (in simultaneous exchange for) payment of some consideration

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: settlement event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: specific event involving the finalization a transaction or portion thereof, including but not limited to finalizing accounting, exchanging consideration, and/or legally recording documents, as applicable

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: settlement terms
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: contract terms that define the commitment to and mechanism for settling one or more sides of a transaction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business center code
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: code used to denote a metropolitan area where business is conducted

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business center code set
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: coding scheme used to define a set of codes for municipalities or business centers

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business day adjustment code
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: code used to denote a convention for specifying what happens when a date falls on a day that is weekend or holiday in some municipality or business center

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business register identifier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: identifier that uniquely identifies a business register, such as a register identified by the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) registration authorities list

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business registration authority
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: registration authority that is responsible for maintaining a registry of business entities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business registry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: registry for registering and maintaining information about business entities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: business registry entry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entry in a business registry

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity expiration reason
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: code for the reason that a legal entity ceased to exist and/or operate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity legal form registry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: registry for registering and maintaining information about the legal forms that are valid for business entities for a particular jurisdiction following the ISO 20275 standard

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity legal form registry entry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entry in an entity legal form registry that conforms to ISO 20275

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity status
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lifecycle stage indicating the operational and/or legal status of an entity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: entity validation level
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: code for the level of validation performed by the GLEIF or LOU with respect to the reference data provided by the registrant

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: legal entity identifier registry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: registry for registering and maintaining information about business entities for a particular jurisdiction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: legal entity identifier registry entry
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: entry in a legal entity identifier registry that conforms to ISO 17442 and the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF) Common Data Format (CDF)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: local operating unit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: registrar that is authorized by the Global LEI Foundation to issue legal entity identifiers

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: North American Industry Classification System code
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code representing an industry

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: North American Industry Classification System scheme
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the scheme defining the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Codes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: registration authority code
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: identifier that uniquely identifies a business registry, and is associated with a registration authority and jurisdiction, issued by the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: registration status
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: lifecycle stage indicating the status of a given registration of something, such as a business or legal entity, as specified by the registration authority

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standard industrial classification code
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the SIC code representing an industry

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: standard industrial classification scheme
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: the scheme defining the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) Code List

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: passport number
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.definition: national identification number associated with a passport

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontolog.label: CRD credit institution
